newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 20.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - May 20.

text.p: Following are some of the leading stories in the Japanese press on Tuesday, as reported by Kyodo news agency.
-- Japan, United States, Britain and other countries have agreed to tighten international surveillance on commodity futures trading.
-- U.S. defense report vows to maintain current troop level in East Asia.
-- Unrecoverable loans at Nippon Credit Bank Ltd to reach 700 billion yen.
-- Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd converted 600 million yen in unpaid interest into unsecured loan for corporate racketeer Ryuichi Koike.
-- Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) panel to propose interest rate increase.
-- Japanese Internet providers to impose voluntary controls on harmful Net messages.
-- Survey shows that four leading brokerages mired in 223 lawsuits totalling 47.2 billion yen for damages across Japan.
-- Japan is not considering joining one trillion yen theater missile defense project.
-- Japan's carbon dioxide emissions worst at 332 million tonnes in the year ended March 1996.
